images.caption: Figure 1:Manga2Animate turns existing manga pages into coherent animation that stays faithful to the original manga.Given a few manga pages(left), our multi-agent framework first builds an animation script and a visual storyboard as intermediate representations, iteratively refining both through creator-reviewer collaboration, and then generates the final animation from them(right). The resulting animation preserves the manga’s plot, character identity, and art style, while flowing coherently from clip to clip.

Figure 2:Limitations of existing methods to manga-to-animation generation.(a) Text-based storytelling methods (AniMaker, ViMax, StoryMem) access the manga mainly through text, losing its art style (1) or distorting characters (2). (b) Feeding manga pages into a video model (e.g., Seedance 2.0) tells the wrong story (3) and shows manga panels as video frames (4).

Figure 3:Overview of the Manga2Animate pipeline.(a) Pre-processing extracts ordered panels, a transcript, and character descriptions. (b) Creator and reviewer agents refine an animation script and a visual storyboard overNNrounds and select the best script and best storyboard, dual-level feedback also guides the next round. (c) Video generation runs in first-frame or reference-conditioned mode.

Figure 4:Compositional (clip-wise) selection by the Script Reviewer.The reviewer selects the best character and clip description at each panel position across theNsN_{s}candidate scripts and reassembles them into one best script (left). For one panel (right), it flags inaccurate details (red) in two candidates and selects the one matching the panel (green).

Figure A1:Correspondence among intermediate representations.Each manga panel(left)corresponds to one clip in the animation script(middle), which describes the environment, character positions, actions, and expressions of that panel in a structured JSON format. Each script clip is then rendered as one storyboard panel(right). In first-frame mode, that panel conditions the corresponding video clip directly; in reference-conditioned mode, the complete storyboard jointly conditions the multi-shot video.
